question.text: In an experiment with a convex lens. The plot of the image distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>'</mo></msup></mfenced></math> against the object distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>'</mo></msup></mfenced></math> measured from the focus gives a curve <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>225</mn></math>. If all the distances are measured in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>. The magnitude of the focal length of the lens is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Using Newton's formula for lenses,

vu=f2 , here, f is focal length of the lens.

Given here, v'μ'=225

Thus, focal length of the lens is f2=225

Or f=15 cm
